newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA cuts banks' prime asset ratio requirement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA cuts banks' prime asset ratio requirement.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia said on Tuesday that it would cut the ratio of commercial banks' funds which has to be kept with the RBA, known as the prime assets ratio, to three percent from six percent.

The RBA also said the range of commercial bank assets which would be eligible for the ratio would be widened to include Australian-dollar denominated securities issued by the central borrowing authorities of state and territory governments.
The Reserve Bank said the changes to PAR had no implications for monetary policy.
The bank said it would confine its transactions in state and territory securities to secondary markets and would not undertake transactions in them directly with issuing authorities.

These changes were taken against a background of diminishing supply of Commonwealth (federal) securities and were part of a refocussing of the RBA's supervision of liquidity to put greater emphasis on banks' internal management prectices, the bank said.

The RBA said TJAT over coming months it would be holding discussions with each bank to agree a liquidity management approach, including overall holdings of liquid assets, taking into account the bank's own methodologies and business characteristics.

The supply of Commonwelth government securities is set to diminish rapidly this year onwards as the federal government plans to transform its budget deficit into a surplus by 1998/99 (to June 30) and deliver further surpluses in the three years following.
